A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same LK-loss study. Their complete main texts, figures, tables, equations, and Appendices A–F are readable and matchable, supporting a reliable comparison.

before.justification: V1 reports original Gaussian-fitting experiments and draft-model evaluations across six target models, four draft architectures, and three benchmarks, including detailed results in Appendix F.

after.justification: V2 retains these original experiments and adds scheduler settings, another checkpoint comparison, and measured wall-clock speedups in Appendix F.

M1.justification: The adaptive KL–TV hybrid, negative log-acceptance objective, stop-gradient scheduler, vocabulary treatment, and draft architectures remain unchanged. Testing additional scheduler coefficients does not introduce a new method component.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same Infinity-Instruct training corpus and MT-Bench, HumanEval, and GSM8K evaluations. Added timing measurements and scheduler settings retain this coverage. Tree sampling and block verification remain proposed future evaluations.

E2.justification: Table 4 adds RedHatAI's Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct-speculator.eagle3 checkpoint, labeled RH-8B, to the Llama-8B comparison. New timing comparisons also use vanilla autoregressive decoding as their reference. Existing loss and checkpoint comparators remain; AdaSPEC is discussed but not evaluated.

E3.justification: V2 adds a tokens-per-second speedup metric against vanilla decoding under matched target-model and hardware configurations, with batch size 1 specified in Table 4. The scheduler sweep additionally tests eta=0.7 and 10. Existing acceptance metrics, temperatures, draft lengths, and training budgets remain unchanged.

E4.justification: Tables 1 and 4 extend the Llama-3.1-8B/EAGLE-3 scheduler sensitivity analysis with eta=0.7 and 10 at both temperatures. This broadens the existing investigation of adaptive blending strength; the Gaussian example, pure-TV comparison, and fixed-mixture ablation are retained.

E5.justification: Neither version reports experimental seed counts, repeated-run counts, confidence intervals, variability estimates, or significance tests. The newly added timing results likewise appear only as point estimates.

E6.justification: Table 4 adds substantial new wall-clock evidence across all six target models; for example, Qwen3 on GSM8K at T=1 reports 2.50× speedup for KL and 2.68× for hybrid LK, with no corresponding timing results in v1. V2 also adds scheduler and RH-8B results and changes ZK-8B's GSM8K acceptance length at T=1 from 3.21 to 3.36. Table 2's numerical results remain unchanged.

T1.justification: The acceptance-rate definitions, loss equations, gradient derivations and scaling analysis, NLL connection, density-overlap argument, and greedy-sampling analysis are unchanged. Appendices A–E are identical. The added speedup metric introduces no new theoretical result.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution bullets, and main conclusion retain the same claims: two acceptance-oriented objectives, applicability across target models and draft architectures, acceptance-length gains up to approximately 8–10%, and integration without additional training overhead.

C2.justification: Section 5.4 changes transfer to other verification schemes from an assertion to an expectation. The expanded limitations discuss untested scheduler alternatives, aggregation order, tree/block verification, and data-diversity versus epoch trade-offs. Future direct optimization shifts from the accepted-to-drafted-token ratio to acceptance length, while the earlier top-k/top-p suggestion disappears.

D1.justification: V2 newly specifies an 8K training sequence length and patched vLLM v0.11.0, noting equivalent upstream sampling support from v0.18.0. Table 4 clarifies that RH-20B uses a checkpoint predating a subsequent weight update. These are disclosures, not evidence that the previously reported training setup or checkpoint weights changed.

R1.justification: Section 2.2 adds AdaSPEC and distinguishes selective distillation of standalone drafters from this work's integrated draft modules. Other reference revisions concern the same works, including the changed author/year attribution for 'Speculative decoding: Performance or illusion?', and do not establish additional literature additions or removals.

P1.justification: V2 locally expands related-work and evaluation explanations, replaces the short future-work paragraph with a longer limitations discussion, and adds an Impact Statement. It also updates publication text, terminology capitalization, and bibliography metadata. The overall section sequence and most prose remain intact.

P2.justification: Table 1 gains scheduler rows. Table 4 pairs acceptance length with speedup, adds rows and bold highlighting, and moves checkpoint identifiers from its caption to a footnote. These are localized display changes; both figures and the mathematical appendix layouts remain unchanged.

improvement.justification: V1 supports practical efficiency primarily through acceptance length; v2 adds measured speedups in Appendix F, broader scheduler checks, and clearer implementation disclosures. Its explicit qualification of transfer beyond chain sampling also improves claim calibration. These are useful gains, but the timing study still omits hardware specifications and run variability, limiting reproducibility and the strength of the added practical evidence.
